latin: Cum dicit Aristoteles nono Methaphysicae separata et diuina aut totaliter sciri a nobis, aut totaliter ignorari, intelligendum est de ea cognitione quae his contingit qui iam ad summam intellectus actuationem peruenerunt.
translation: When Aristotle says, in the ninth book of the Metaphysics, that separate and divine things are either wholly known by us or wholly unknown, this must be understood of the cognition available to those who have already attained the highest actuation of the intellect.
